content:
Vanessa Ortiz: heads up on something we’re seeing in staging + worried about for Dedicated: when we do stage-based traffic shifting (5% -> 25% -> 100%) on a reserved pool, utilization doesn’t behave linearly. 5% can still spike GPU util / queue depth enough to blow SLO if the canary pods are “cold” (KV cache empty) or we get unlucky w/ long-context requests. anyone else seeing this?

Elena Popov: yeah. deterministic routing means that 5% of hashes can be “heavier” than average depending on tenant traffic shape. esp if tenant has a few giant customers and hashing is per end-user id. even if it’s per request id, the *warmup* period still hurts.

Keiko Yamamoto: +1. also reserved pools often run closer to the edge by design (cost). during partial rollout, you effectively create two fleets inside one pool: old replicas + new replicas. new replicas start with worse throughput (no warmed cache, sometimes different quant profile), so same QPS burns more GPU.

Mina Haddad: routing side: stage weights are correct, but we don’t currently enforce “capacity headroom before shifting”. we basically assume pool can absorb the shift. we should not assume that for Dedicated.

Irene Choi: this matches what we saw during last month’s model swap for Acme Dedicated. the pool was at ~70-75% util steady state. we shifted 10% traffic, new pods were slower, util jumped to 95% and queue depth ran away. autoscaler couldn’t help because reserved pool size is fixed + we only have burst sometimes.

Vanessa Ortiz: exactly. the scary part: even with burst enabled, spin-up time means we’re already in the red by the time extra GPUs arrive.

Sean Gallagher: from SRE side, I’m going to be cranky if we allow stage progression without explicit guardrails. “5%” isn’t a safety mechanism if 5% can saturate. needs a precheck gate.

Keiko Yamamoto: proposal: minimum headroom rule tied to *effective capacity*, not raw GPU count. e.g. before advancing stage, require:
- avg GPU util < 70% over last N mins
- p95 queue depth < X (or queue delay < Y)
- and a “projected headroom” calc: `headroom = 1 - (current_load / expected_capacity_after_shift)`

Mina Haddad: where would that live? evaluator can compute it (gate), but we also need to *block routing change* if the precheck isn’t met.

Elena Popov: evaluator should gate stage advance, but also we should consider adding a rate limiter on weight changes. like max +5% per 5 minutes even if stage is configured as 25%. stage could be “target 25%” but applied as ramp.

Vanessa Ortiz: ramp inside a stage seems good. otherwise ppl will config stage 2 = 25% and we’ll jump immediately.

Ravi Menon: careful: product is calling this “deterministic staged rollouts”, but we can still do deterministic + ramp (deterministic hash ring update in small deltas). we just need to make sure the allocation is stable per step.

Logan Wright: metrics side: we can give you GPU util + queue depth + timeout rate with low cardinality at (tenant,pool) level. but “expected_capacity_after_shift” is tricky b/c new version performance is unknown. can approximate using token/sec per replica from recent window, but cold start skews it.

Keiko Yamamoto: that’s the point: cold start is the hazard. maybe guardrail should explicitly include “warmup” period:
- hold new replicas at 0% for W mins while they preload weights + compile kernels
- then allow traffic

Mina Haddad: can we warm them without traffic? KV cache won’t warm, but we can at least ensure model load/compile is done and that healthchecks are passing.

Irene Choi: we already see that first 3-5 mins after spin-up are slow: weight load + graph compilation. so a “Stage 0 shadow / preload” makes sense.

Vanessa Ortiz: but shadow traffic in Dedicated is… not always possible? we can’t duplicate traffic for some tenants due to policy.

Ravi Menon: we can do “dry run readiness” (load + compile + basic canary prompt) without customer traffic. not perfect but better than flipping 5% onto pods still compiling.

Sean Gallagher: + require manual approval on first customer-facing stage for beta. and default evaluation window >= 10 min. our current thinking of 2-3 min windows will false-pass.

Elena Popov: another risk: if pool is heterogeneous (some A100s + some H100s) or mixed MIG shapes, the “new” rollout might land disproportionately on a subset w/ different perf. then 5% becomes “all on the slowest slice”.

Keiko Yamamoto: agreed. guardrail should include “placement sanity”: ensure new replicas are spread across fault domains + HW types.

Vanessa Ortiz: on reserved pools we sometimes pin to specific nodes for isolation. spreading is limited.

Irene Choi: still can enforce “don’t place all new replicas on one rack / one host group”.

Logan Wright: for gating we can also look at “util delta” immediately after shift. like “if util increases > 15pp within 2 mins, auto-hold”. that’s a good generic signal.

Mina Haddad: that’s implementable. evaluator can compare pre/post windows. but note: traffic can be bursty naturally.

Sean Gallagher: then use queue delay + error rate as confirmers. utilization alone might be noisy.

Keiko Yamamoto: autoscaling guardrail idea: if burst capacity is enabled, stage advancement should *request* burst first and wait for it to be ready before increasing weight. i.e. pre-scale, then shift.

Vanessa Ortiz: yes please. right now burst is reactive.

Irene Choi: also: if no burst, then “min headroom” should be stricter. like require util < 60% before moving beyond 25%.

Ravi Menon: can we encode this as:
- policy: `min_headroom_percent` per stage
- evaluator computes current headroom = f(util, queue)
- routing refuses to apply new weights unless evaluator says OK

Elena Popov: routing refusing is good for safety but needs to be explainable in UI. otherwise operators think it’s stuck.

Vanessa Ortiz: yup. UI should show: “Blocked by headroom guardrail: util 82% > 70% threshold”

CapacityBot: (auto) Staging pool `ded-pool-stg-07` queue_depth p95 exceeded threshold (p95=41, threshold=25) for 6m. Related dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ded-pool-stg-07/queue

Mina Haddad: lol bot timing is perfect.

Keiko Yamamoto: another concrete guardrail: limit the absolute number of new-version replicas in a pool unless there’s headroom. ex: stage 1 might be 5% but if pool is tiny (8 GPUs), 5% maps to 1 replica and that 1 replica can be a single point of overload. we should ensure minimum replica count for a stage or not allow stage configs on small pools.

Irene Choi: +1. “1 replica canary” on a high-QPS tenant is basically guaranteed to queue.

Sean Gallagher: in those cases better to do request sampling to canary without hard-pinning all canary traffic to 1 replica. but we’re not there yet.

Ravi Menon: deterministic allocation currently operates at request->version mapping, not replica. but if only 1 replica serves new version, it’s effectively pinned. so add requirement: stage must have >=k replicas for new version OR stage weight must be 0.

Vanessa Ortiz: can we define k=2 default? plus “canary must not exceed 50% util on canary slice” (if we can measure it).

Logan Wright: measuring per-version util in a shared pool is possible if we add a `model_version` label, but that’s cardinality risk. we were planning a low-card approach: emit per (pool, rollout_id, stage_id) aggregate rather than per model.

Mina Haddad: that works. we just need *some* way to see canary slice health.

Keiko Yamamoto: ok, summarizing guardrail proposals (v1):
1) Preload/compile hold: new replicas must be Ready for >= W mins before any weight > 0
2) Min headroom gate: require util + queue delay below thresholds before advancing
3) Ramp within stage: apply weight changes gradually (delta cap)
4) Pre-scale burst (if enabled) before weight increase
5) Min replica count for canary slice on small pools
6) Placement spread check (best-effort)

Vanessa Ortiz: + “auto-hold on missing metrics” — if we can’t see queue/util, do NOT advance.

Sean Gallagher: yes. fail-safe = pause.

Elena Popov: question: where does “delta cap” live? evaluator can output “recommended applied weight” vs “target stage weight”? or routing layer enforces cap regardless of plan.

Ravi Menon: I’d put cap in routing/policy so it’s not optional. evaluator still decides “advance stage” but routing controls how fast we move toward target weight.

Mina Haddad: ok but then stage semantics become fuzzy. stage says 25% but actual is 10% for a while. that’s fine as long as UI reflects “in ramp”.

Irene Choi: ops will like “in ramp” more than “it jumped and we died”.

Logan Wright: if we do ramp, we need a metric for “applied_weight” vs “target_weight” so gates don’t evaluate wrong window.

Keiko Yamamoto: I can write up a quick note for ENG-5130 (autoscaling guardrails) with these bullets + suggested defaults. want owners?

Vanessa Ortiz: Keiko + Irene can you take first pass? I’ll add Dedicated ops constraints (fixed pool size, burst timing, small pool edge cases).

Sean Gallagher: loop me in for threshold defaults + SLO alignment.

Mina Haddad: I’ll sync with routing team on where delta cap belongs. we need this before beta.

Keiko Yamamoto: cool. will draft today and drop link here.

Keiko Yamamoto: draft doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/x/ded-rollout-headroom-guardrails (WIP). pls comment esp on stage ramp + min replicas.

Vanessa Ortiz: reading now. :thumbsup:

Irene Choi: added a note on burst: we need an explicit “burst_ready” signal from fleet manager, not just “requested”. otherwise we’ll still advance too early.

Logan Wright: commented w/ metrics availability + suggested eval windows (10m steady + 2m step-change detector). also flagged cardinality if we label by model_version.

Sean Gallagher: added SRE note: default action on gate fail should be HOLD not ROLLBACK for capacity signals (rollback only if sustained error/timeout). for queue/util spikes, rollback can make things worse if it causes reload churn.

Mina Haddad: good point. rollback thrash is real.

Vanessa Ortiz: ok this is great. next step: align w/ control plane team that “headroom gate” is mandatory for Dedicated staged rollouts. I’ll ping Ethan separately.

CapacityBot: (auto) `ded-pool-stg-07` queue_depth p95 recovered (p95=18) after mitigation (traffic shift aborted).
